rule: `ToString` is invoked implicitly inside string interpolation via virtual dispatch for present values; `StringBuilder.Append(value: Object)` keeps `value.ToString()`'s text.

title: a nullable function-typed local renders its function type or null at an interpolation hole
rule: For function values the ToString rendering is the stdlib 2.13 FullName of the value's own function type, "(int) -> int", parameter names not rendered; a null hole renders as the four characters null (spec 18.5, 8.5).

title: a call returning a null function-typed value renders null at a hole
rule: A null hole renders as the four characters null with no dispatch; a nullable function-typed call result that is null is such a hole (spec 8.5, 18.5).

title: a function-typed field read renders its function type or null at a hole
rule: For function values the ToString rendering is the stdlib 2.13 FullName of the value's own function type, "(int) -> int"; a null hole renders null (spec 8.5).

title: a null-conditional read of a function-typed field renders null or the function type
rule: For function values the ToString rendering is the stdlib 2.13 FullName of the value's own function type; a null hole (here the short-circuited ?. result) renders null (spec 8.5, 18.5).

title: ToString() on an owning choice with no declared ToString is a use-site compile error
rule: For a choice that is owning (no default is generated), a ToString() call at a statically-known receiver type is a use-site compile error, removed by declaring the member (spec 8.5, 35.7, v0.350).

title: boxing of a class, record, string, int, nullable int and value-like choice to Console members ...
rule: Value-like auto-hashable choices, classes, records and integers box and render normally (spec 8.5, 35.8, v0.350): a class renders by its declared ToString, a positional record as Rec(x: 3), a value-like choice as TypeName.CaseName;

title: a class without ToString renders as its qualified name and a positional record as its field listing
rule: For classes the default is the type's qualified name ("M.Res" in module M); for positional records a representation of fields (spec 8.5, v0.350).

title: WriteLine of a [2]string through a TextWriter local renders the type name
rule: For inline arrays (all forms, including move-only `[N owned]…` arrays, whose receiver is borrowed for the call) and for the unit type: the type's name — `"[3]int"`-style for an inline array

title: WriteLine of a [2]string straight on Console.Out renders the same type name
rule: For inline arrays (all forms, including move-only `[N owned]…` arrays, whose receiver is borrowed for the call) and for the unit type: the type's name — `"[3]int"`-style for an inline array

title: a nullable-element inline array renders [3]int? through ToString and as an Object
rule: For inline arrays (all forms, including move-only `[N owned]…` arrays, whose receiver is borrowed for the call) and for the unit type: the type's name — `"[3]int"`-style for an inline array

title: a stdlib enum renders its qualified type name through Object, a nullable hole, and null as "null"
rule: and for enums: the type's qualified name

title: an enum declaring ToString replaces the default for direct, boxed and interpolated use
rule: An enum may replace its default by declaring a `ToString(): string` member

title: a generic hole and a concatenated ToString render stdlib and user enums by qualified name
rule: and for enums: the type's qualified name

title: a move-only owning inline array cannot be boxed
rule: Move-only value types — owning inline arrays (`[N owned]T` and `[N owned]T?`) — cannot be boxed. Boxing a value type copies the value into a heap wrapper, but move-only types forbid copying.

title: a non-owning inline array boxes per the general rule
rule: Non-owning inline arrays (`[N]T` and `[N]T?`) are ordinary value types and box per the general rule.

title: boxing a nullable value type yields a null reference or a boxed non-nullable
rule: When a nullable value type `T?` is boxed: if the value is `null`, the result is a null `Object` reference; if the value is non-null, the result is a boxed `T` — the nullable wrapper is stripped during boxing.

title: a boxed borrow-bearing record may not be stored in a field
rule: The compiler enforces: a boxed borrow-bearing record value may not be stored in a location that could outlive the source of any borrow the record contains. The boxed copy on the heap holds the same borrowed references as the source record; it does not extend their lifetimes.

title: a span passed to a parameter declared Object is rejected at the conversion
rule: So a value that holds borrows (§3.6) is converted to `Object` or to an interface type at exactly one position: as the receiver of a member call ... Every other conversion — at a parameter, plain or `scoped` (§28.14), declared `Object` or any other interface type, or at a bare type parameter the call substitutes with one (`b.Keep<Object>(span)`); at a local, a field, a collection slot or collection-literal element, a record component, a choice payload, an inline-array slot, a `ref` or `out` location, or a `return`, by an implicit conversion or by an `as` or a typed pattern at such a type — is a compile error at the conversion

title: a span bound to a local declared Object is rejected at the conversion
rule: So a value that holds borrows (§3.6) is converted to `Object` or to an interface type at exactly one position: as the receiver of a member call ... Every other conversion — at a parameter, plain or `scoped` (§28.14), declared `Object` or any other interface type, or at a bare type parameter the call substitutes with one (`b.Keep<Object>(span)`); at a local, a field, a collection slot or collection-literal element, a record component, a choice payload, an inline-array slot, a `ref` or `out` location, or a `return`, by an implicit conversion or by an `as` or a typed pattern at such a type — is a compile error at the conversion

title: a span passed to Console.WriteLine's Object overload is rejected
rule: This is the twin of §28.3's *Set-erasing positions* for a function value, and rejects the same short list of non-storing calls: `Console.WriteLine(span)` and `StringBuilder.Append(span)` at their `Object` parameters, whose spelling is `span.ToString()` or an interpolation hole

title: rendering a span through its own ToString member call is admitted
rule: The remedies at a rejected conversion are a parameter or local declared at the value's own type (a member that accepts a read-only span of either heap backing declares one overload per span type, stdlib §4.14), a class implementing the target interface, or — for rendering — `x.ToString()` or an interpolation hole, which invoke a member on the value

title: a borrow-bearing record as the receiver of an extension on a user interface is rejected
rule: The receiver of an extension-block call whose head is `Object` or an interface type is not admitted: that body reads `this` at the head type, which announces no borrow, and may pass it to a parameter that stores it (§28.3's field-store bullet), so the receiver position is borrow-erasing like a parameter of that type.

title: a record holding no borrow boxes as the receiver of an extension on a user interface
rule: When a value type is used where `Object` (or an interface implemented by the value type) is expected, the value is boxed: a heap-allocated wrapper holds the value.

title: an owning inline array cannot be boxed to Object
rule: Boxing copies, and a move-only value type (an owning inline array) cannot be copied, so it cannot be boxed (spec 8.6 and 15.3, v0.350); passing it where Object is expected, as Console.WriteLine does, is rejected.

title: Dispose through a nullable Object-typed receiver is rejected
rule: `Dispose()` is class-only. (§8.7, v0.340) `Object` is not a class that generates `IDisposable`: the statement `o?.Dispose()` over `o: Object?` names no member `Dispose` of `Object`.

title: Dispose through an Object-typed receiver holding a value is rejected
rule: `Dispose()` is class-only. (§8.7, v0.340) `Object` is not a class that generates `IDisposable`: the call `q.Dispose()` over `q: Object` (holding a boxed int) names no member `Dispose` of `Object`.

title: Dispose on a user class through a null-conditional receiver is accepted
rule: The compiler generates `IDisposable` on every non-static class. (§8.7, v0.340) The user class `D` declares no `Dispose`, yet `d?.Dispose()` over `d: D?` is a call of the generated member and compiles and runs.

title: Dispose on standard-library classes is accepted, directly and through a null-conditional receiver
rule: The compiler generates `IDisposable` on every non-static class. (§8.7, v0.340) `Mutex` and `FileStream` are classes, so `m.Dispose()` and `f?.Dispose()` over a null `FileStream?` compile and run.

title: the universal members ToString, Equals and GetHashCode remain on Object
rule: Only `Dispose()` is "not on `Object`" (§8.7, v0.340); the members every `Object` carries (§8.1: `ToString`, `Equals`, `GetHashCode`) are still declared: for a class instance held as `Object`, `ToString().Length > 0`, `Equals(o)` of itself and a stable hash code all hold.

title: Dispose on a user interface that does not extend IDisposable is a compile error
rule: Language spec §8.7 (v0.345): "On `Object`, on a runtime-managed value and on a value of any other interface type … a user interface that neither extends `IDisposable` nor declares the member — the name resolves to no member, so a call in any spelling (`x.Dispose()`, `x?.Dispose()`, `x!.Dispose()`) … are compile errors at the type level".

title: DisposeAsync on a user interface that does not extend IAsyncDisposable is a compile error
rule: Language spec §8.7 (v0.345): "`DisposeAsync()` is a member only of a type that declares or inherits it — `IAsyncDisposable`, the interfaces extending it, a class implementing it".

title: Dispose is a member of an interface that extends IDisposable
rule: Language spec §8.7 (v0.345): "`Dispose()` is a member of a class type, of an interface type that is or extends `IDisposable` — the interfaces `where T: IDisposable` admits … and of nothing else".

title: a positional record generates a primary constructor and read-only properties
rule: For each positional record, the compiler generates a primary constructor whose parameters are the positional fields, in declaration order, and public read-only properties, one per positional field, with the same names.

title: the auto-generated positional properties read back the constructor arguments
rule: A record may declare positional fields in parentheses after its name; the compiler generates a primary constructor whose parameters are the positional fields and public read-only properties with the same names.

title: positional-record equality compares all positional fields
rule: Value equality (=, <>) is based on all positional fields (those marked equality skip excepted), generated only when every participating positional field is of an admissible component type.

title: positional-record ToString renders TypeName(Field1 colon value1, ...)
rule: ToString is formatted as "TypeName(Field1: value1, Field2: value2)".

title: comparing a positional record with an inadmissible field type is rejected at the call site
rule: A positional record with an inadmissible field declares fine, but comparing it is a compile error rather than silent reference equality.

title: comparing a positional record with an admissible field type is accepted
rule: Value equality is generated when every participating positional field is of an admissible component type; comparing such a record is unrestricted.

title: a body record with only auto-properties and a method is auto-hashable
rule: A body-only record receives auto-generated =, <>, GetHashCode, and ToString over its auto-properties when every instance member is an admissible auto-property, a method, a computed property, an eligible operator overload, or a constructor.

title: auto-generated body-record ToString lists auto-properties in declaration order
rule: The generated ToString produces "TypeName(Prop1: value1, Prop2: value2)" over the auto-properties in declaration order.

title: computed properties are excluded from auto-equality and auto-ToString
rule: Computed (expression-bodied) properties are not part of the equality comparison or the ToString output even when they are visible on the public surface; equality and the auto-formatted representation are always over storage, never over derived values.

title: primitive, enum, string, and nullable components are all admissible
rule: Admissible component types include a primitive type, an enum, or string, and T? where T is admissible, compared by the null-safe = of section 8.4.

title: another auto-hashable record is an admissible component type
rule: Admissible component types include another record that is itself auto-hashable, applied recursively.

title: a non-owning inline array of admissible element type is an admissible component
rule: Admissible component types include a non-owning inline array [N]T or [N]T? whose element type is admissible, compared element-by-element.

title: an auto-hashable value-like choice is an admissible component type
rule: Admissible component types include a value-like choice that is itself auto-hashable, per section 35.7, recursively applying this same list to every case's payload fields.

title: an explicit field declaration disqualifies auto-hashable and equality use is rejected
rule: A body record is not auto-hashable when it contains an explicit field declaration (storage that is not an auto-property), unless the field is marked equality skip; = on such a record without an explicit overload is a compile error.

title: equality skip on an explicit field rescues auto-hashable
rule: A storage component marked equality skip is removed from the auto-equality membership computation; a member whose type is inadmissible, including an explicit field declaration, does not disqualify the record when marked equality skip.

title: overriding Equals and GetHashCode disqualifies auto-hashable and equality use is rejected
rule: An `override` of `Equals` or `GetHashCode` ... Declaring either means the author has taken over equality ... the record is therefore not auto-hashable ... and `=`/`<>` are a compile error unless the author also declares the `operator =`/`<>` overloads

title: declaring the operator overloads beside an Equals or GetHashCode override restores equality use
rule: = and <> on a record outside the auto-hashable set are a compile error unless the author also declares the operator =/<> overloads, along with Equals(T) and GetHashCode overrides as needed.

title: a homogeneous equality overload disqualifies auto-hashable and an undeclared Equals use is rejected
rule: A homogeneous operator =/<> overload disqualifies the record from auto-hashable; calling someRecord.Equals(other) on a non-auto-hashable record without a user-defined declaration of that member — the `override` spelling or the plain one — is a compile error. The error fires per member: Money declares Equals(Money) and not Equals(Object?), and the Object?-argument call is the member it does not declare.

title: declaring Equals(T) beside a homogeneous equality overload makes the direct call legal
rule: The compile error on a non-auto-hashable record covers Equals(T) and GetHashCode; it fires per member and a user-defined declaration of that member — the `override` spelling or the plain one — removes it for that member. (An Equals taking Object? is rejected on a record, §9.2.)

title: a zero-auto-property body record compares equal always and renders TypeName()
rule: A body-only record with zero auto-properties is auto-hashable; the generated = returns true for every pair of values, and the generated ToString produces "TypeName()".

title: virtual is rejected on a record member
rule: A record member may not be declared virtual, abstract, or sealed override (v0.297); record members are always dispatched statically.

title: abstract is rejected on a record member
rule: A record member may not be declared virtual, abstract, or sealed override (v0.297); record members are always dispatched statically.

title: sealed override is rejected on a record member
rule: A record member may not be declared virtual, abstract, or sealed override (v0.297); bare sealed on any member is already section 12.4's error, and this rule adds sealed override.

title: override is admitted on ToString and replaces the compiler-generated rendering
rule: override is admitted only on Equals, GetHashCode, and ToString; an override here names the Object slot the member fills and implies no chain.

title: override is rejected on a record member other than Equals, GetHashCode, or ToString
rule: override is admitted only on Equals, GetHashCode, and ToString, and is rejected on every other record member, whatever its kind: method, property, or indexer.

title: equality skip on a static field is an inert-annotation compile error
rule: The equality skip clause is admitted on storage components only; on a static member it is a compile error, mirroring section 9.8's inert-annotation rule, because a static member never participates in equality.

title: an override Equals at Object? on a record is rejected at the declaration
rule: An `Equals` taking `Object?` or `Object` is rejected on every value kind at the declaration, `override` or plain, the diagnostic naming the own-typed spelling

title: a plain Equals at Object? on a record is rejected at the declaration
rule: An `Equals` taking `Object?` or `Object` is rejected on every value kind at the declaration, `override` or plain, the diagnostic naming the own-typed spelling

title: a record declaring a plain own-typed Equals and no GetHashCode is rejected
rule: On a value kind — a record, an enum or a choice — whose `Object`-slot `Equals` takes its own type and is declared `override` or plain, the two spellings declaring one member ... the rule reads both spellings of both members: a plain `Equals` obliges `GetHashCode`, and a plain `GetHashCode` discharges the obligation.

title: a plain GetHashCode beside a plain own-typed Equals discharges the obligation on a record
rule: On a value kind — a record, an enum or a choice — whose `Object`-slot `Equals` takes its own type and is declared `override` or plain, the two spellings declaring one member ... the rule reads both spellings of both members: a plain `Equals` obliges `GetHashCode`, and a plain `GetHashCode` discharges the obligation.

title: a boxed record declaring only its own-typed Equals compares by that member
rule: On a record that is not auto-hashable, such a call reaches, member by member, the record's own declaration of `Equals` — the own-typed member, which is its `Object` slot ... a boxed `T` argument compares by it on the box's payload, any other argument, `null` included, unequal

title: an Object?-argument Equals through a type parameter reaches a record's own-typed Equals
rule: At a record, an enum or a choice S, the first kind reaches S's own-typed `Equals`, declared or generated — its `Object` slot ...; the second kind reaches the same member through the slot: an argument that is a boxed S compares by it on the box's payload, and any other argument, `null` included, compares unequal

title: a record declaring GetHashCode and no Equals rejects a direct Equals call
rule: Calling `someRecord.Equals(other)` or `someRecord.GetHashCode()` on a non-auto-hashable record without a user-defined declaration of that member — the `override` spelling or the plain one — is a compile error ... The error is per member

title: a record declaring GetHashCode and no Equals admits a direct GetHashCode call
rule: Calling `someRecord.Equals(other)` or `someRecord.GetHashCode()` on a non-auto-hashable record without a user-defined declaration of that member — the `override` spelling or the plain one — is a compile error ... The error is per member

title: a record's own-typed Equals fills the Object slot when a ref-mode Equals overload follows it
rule: On every value kind the `Equals` is the one taking the kind's own type ... declared `override` or plain ...: the one member that fills the kind's `Object` slot ([§9.2]); "overloads differing in any of these are distinguishable", and the `ref`/`out` modifiers are one of them ([§22.6]), so `Equals(ref other: R)` is an ordinary second overload.

title: an IEquatable<R> call on a record reaches the record's own-typed Equals
rule: An interface member at that signature — and one at `GetHashCode(): int` or `ToString(): string` — is satisfied by the kind's own member for that slot, declared or generated ([§9.2], [§14.2]).

title: a boxed generic record with a declared Equals answers through its Object slot, not by reference
rule: On a record that is **not** auto-hashable, such a call reaches, member by member, the record's own declaration of `Equals` — "the own-typed member, which is its `Object` slot" ([§9.2]): "a boxed `T` argument compares by it on the box's payload". The record `R<T>` declares `Equals(other: R<T>)` and so is not auto-hashable; `o.Equals(b)` through the `Object`-typed box reaches that declaration, which returns `true` for every argument.

title: a record's Equals may not take Object? because its Object slot is own-typed
rule: On every value kind the `Equals` is the one taking the kind's own type ([§9.2]), and "no value kind declares an `Equals` at `Object?`" ([§9.2]). The record declares `public method Equals(o: Object?): bool => true;` on line 7, which is not its own-typed `Equals`, so the compiler rejects the declaration. The second diagnostic (the `hashable` requirement of `Contains`) follows from the same record and is not needed for the reject.

title: = between two unrelated record types compares unequal through the Object slot
rule: `a = b` invokes `a.Equals(b)`, with a null-safe wrapper ([§8.4]), and "`<>` is the negation." ([§8.4]). The argument `q` is a `Q`, not a `P`, so the call reaches the Object slot, where "the member runs only on a `T` payload and any other argument compares unequal without the body running" ([§9.2]). So `p = q` is False and `p <> q` is True.

title: a record may combine positional fields with a body that adds further members
rule: A record may have both positional fields and a body; the auto-generated members are present and the body adds further members.

title: a combined-form body may not repeat the auto-generated primary constructor's parameter list
rule: The body may not declare a constructor with the same parameter list as the auto-generated primary constructor.

title: a combined-form body may not declare a property with a positional field's auto-generated name
rule: The body may not declare a property with the same name as a positional field's auto-generated property.

title: a record declaring positional fields may not declare a constructor carrying a contract clause
rule: The body may not declare a constructor carrying a contract clause; the auto-generated primary constructor can carry none, so no record declaring positional fields is constructor-only.

title: a positional field marked equality skip is excluded from equality but still constructed and rendered
rule: A positional field may carry equality skip; the field is excluded from equality but present, constructed, and rendered, and a skipped field's inadmissible type does not disqualify the record.

title: a positional record declaring plain Equals and GetHashCode keeps neither generated member
rule: a disqualifying body member (an `Equals`/`GetHashCode` override, a homogeneous `=`/`<>` overload, or any other member outside the §9.2 list) suppresses the auto-generated equality members ... An `override` of `Equals` or `GetHashCode`, either spelling being the override

title: body-form properties may be declared with any mutability
rule: In the body form, properties may be declared with any mutability. Mutable records are permitted but are inadvisable.

title: a bare store resolving to the receiver's own storage is rejected in a record method body
rule: this binds a borrow of the receiver value; a store that would land in the receiver's own storage is a compile error at the member body, including a bare X := e resolving to the receiver's storage.

title: a compound assignment to receiver storage is rejected through its desugaring
rule: The rule keys on where the store would land; a compound assignment or ++/-- classifies through its section 6.6/17.6 desugaring as a store landing in the receiver's own storage.

title: constructor bodies are not receiver positions
rule: Constructor bodies are not receiver positions; a record constructor initializes the value under construction, and Width := width; is section 9.2's own canonical body-record initialization form.

title: an external store through a named binding on a settable auto-property remains legal
rule: Settable properties keep their purpose: an external store through a named binding's lvalue chain, such as r.X := 5 on a settable auto-property, remains legal, the store landing in r's storage, announced by the assignment itself.

title: a store that hops through a class-typed member leaves the receiver and is legal
rule: A chain that hops through a class- or interface-typed member leaves the receiver: a record's reference-typed fields are borrows, so a store beyond such a hop lands in the borrowed heap object, not in the receiver, and is legal.

title: a this-rooted chain to receiver storage passed as an out argument is the same store by other syntax
rule: A this-rooted chain reaching the receiver's own storage passed as a ref/out argument is the same store by other syntax; an out argument may be a property with an accessible setter.

title: a binding read of an owning inline array field faults after its holder is destroyed
rule: A move-only value disposed in place **with no replacement** — ... or the holder of either kind destroyed (§28.4 step 2, whose per-slot pass disposes an owning inline array's slots in place, §15.1.1) — is left in a **disposed state** ... In checked disposal mode a read of the value in that state — through an in-place `this`, or through a borrowing-match binding of it, an owning inline array's slot reads, iteration and compiler-provided operations (§15.1.2) included — faults as `DisposedAccessException`

title: the same slot read through the binding with the holder alive reads the slot
rule: A move-only value disposed in place **with no replacement** — ... or the holder of either kind destroyed (§28.4 step 2 ...) — is left in a **disposed state**

title: with produces a copy with named fields replaced
rule: A with expression produces a new record value with named fields replaced; the original record value is unchanged.

title: with applies to a freshly constructed record value
rule: new Point(1, 2) with(Y := 9) has a record-typed source and is an ordinary record with applied to the freshly-constructed value; the discriminator is the source expression's type kind, never the presence of new.

title: with over a class-typed source is rejected
rule: The source expression must be record-typed; a with expression whose source is class-typed is a compile error naming this rule, the retired object-initializer reading.

title: a with target must be accessible at the use site under its declared accessibility
rule: A with target must be accessible at the use site under the member's own declared accessibility; a private auto-property is a valid target only inside the declaring record.

title: a with target that is a private auto-property is legal from inside the declaring record
rule: A private auto-property is a valid with target inside the declaring record.

title: with does not re-invoke the constructor and so does not re-validate cross-field invariants
rule: with copies field values directly; it does not invoke the record's constructor. A constructor that validates cross-field invariants is not re-run during with.

title: with over a constructor-only record's source is rejected
rule: A with expression whose source expression's static type is a constructor-only record is a compile error at the with expression, naming the property and the source type.

title: a with over an is-narrowed nullable carrier is the non-nullable record type
rule: The result has the same static type as the source (§9.5, v0.340); and when a test succeeds and the tested expression is one of §7.4's narrowing carriers, "the carrier is flow-narrowed to `T` within the controlled block" (§12.7, v0.340). So a `P?` carrier narrowed by an `is P` test has source type `P` inside the block, the `with` result has type `P`, and a `P` target accepts it; the replaced field takes the named value and the other fields keep the source's values (§9.5).

title: a with over a plain non-nullable record source keeps the other fields' values
rule: The `with` operation constructs the copy directly from the source's storage and "All other fields keep their values from the source record" (§9.5, v0.340). So a `with` over a plain, non-nullable record source replaces only the named field — including a nested record field, which is copied whole and not unwrapped.

title: a record may implement an interface and provide the matching member
rule: A record may implement any number of interfaces that declare no settable property or indexer member.

title: a record cannot derive from another record
rule: A record cannot derive from another record or from a class (other than the implicit Object root).

title: a record cannot implement an interface that declares a settable property
rule: A record may implement any number of interfaces that declare no settable property or indexer member; a conformance naming an interface with one is rejected at the declaration, since a value kind supplies no receiver-storing accessor.

title: a record may implement an interface whose members are all read-only or methods
rule: A record may implement any number of interfaces that declare no settable property or indexer member.

title: a record cannot declare an owned field
rule: Records cannot have destructors, owned fields, or implement IDisposable.

title: a record cannot declare a destructor
rule: Records cannot have destructors, owned fields, or implement IDisposable.

title: a plain reference-typed field in a record is a borrow, not an owned obligation
rule: Reference-typed fields in records are always borrows; the record does not own what they point to.

title: a record whose only reference-typed field is a string is not borrow-bearing
rule: A record whose only reference-typed fields are of declared runtime-managed types (string, function types) is not a borrow-bearing record; runtime-managed values have unbounded lifetime by construction, so no borrow-lifetime rules apply.

title: a borrow-bearing record may not be stored in a non-null static field
rule: A borrow-bearing record may not be stored in a static field of any type, except when every reference-typed field of the value is null.

title: a borrow-bearing record may not be constructed from a temporary
rule: A borrow-bearing record may not be constructed from a temporary bound to one of its borrow-carrying fields; a construction argument that is a fresh call result not bound to a named location has a lifetime that ends at the construction expression.

title: a borrow-bearing record may not be stored in an instance field of a class
rule: A borrow-bearing record value may not be stored in an instance field of a class; a class instance's lifetime is not bounded by any borrow source's scope, so the store is rejected statically.

title: a borrow-bearing record in the null-source form may be stored in a static field
rule: A borrow-bearing record may not be stored in a static field of any type, except when every reference-typed field (and every reference-typed slot of every inline-array field) of the value is null — the null-source form.

title: borrow-carrying is transitive through another borrow-bearing record field
rule: A field is borrow-carrying when its type is another borrow-bearing record, or a borrow-bearing choice (transitivity); such a record is itself borrow-bearing and may not be stored in an instance field of a class.

title: a record of runtime-managed fields is not borrow-bearing under transitivity
rule: A record whose only reference-typed fields are of declared runtime-managed types (`string`, function types) is not a borrow-bearing record, so a record holding one is not borrow-carrying through the transitivity clause either, and no borrow-lifetime rule applies.

title: a borrow-bearing record carrying a borrow of a local may not be returned
rule: A borrow-bearing record may not be returned from a method whose return-type rules cannot establish a sufficient lifetime for every borrow the record carries.

title: a null-source borrow-bearing record value carries no borrow and may be returned
rule: A borrow-bearing record may not be returned from a method whose return-type rules cannot establish a sufficient lifetime for every borrow the record carries; a null-source value — every reference-typed field null — carries none.

title: the static null-source quantifier reaches every reference-typed field
rule: The quantifier is over reference-typed fields, not over borrow-carrying fields alone: a field whose declared type is reference-typed but not borrow-carrying — a `string`, a function type — must be null too. `record Tok(Src: Object?, Name: string)` initialized `new Tok(null, "missing")` is therefore rejected.

title: a value whose every reference-typed field is null satisfies the quantifier
rule: The quantifier is over reference-typed fields, not over borrow-carrying fields alone, so a null-source value holds no reference of any kind. At `Name: string?`, `new Tok(null, null)` is admitted as a static.

title: a record-carried borrow may not be copied into a longer-lived collection
rule: A borrow-bearing record value may be copied into a collection only when every carried borrow's source provably outlives the collection's own binding scope; a store into a collection whose binding's scope strictly encloses a carried source's scope is rejected at the store site.

title: a record-carried borrow whose source outlives the collection may be copied in
rule: A borrow-bearing record value may be copied into a collection when every carried borrow's source provably outlives the collection's own binding scope; the check is the same structural scope comparison as section 28.3's borrow rules.

title: an owned T return of an owned parameter is rejected at a borrow-bearing record substitution
rule: Over `record Pair(Item: Item)`, `static method Pass<T>(owned a: T): owned T => a;` is therefore rejected at `Pass<Pair>`, its return carrying a borrow of an `owned` parameter, and so are ... and `static method Id<T>(a: T): T where T: value => a;` at `Id<Pair>`; each stays admitted at the declaration and at every substitution that carries no borrow.

title: an owned T factory whose fresh result carries no borrow is admitted at a borrow-bearing record
rule: The rejection is per return expression, never at the declaration ... In a generic body this bullet reaches the return of a member declared to return `owned T` for a bare type parameter `T` ... it is checked at each instantiation substituting for it a value type that holds borrows

title: a where T: value identity is rejected at a borrow-bearing record substitution
rule: Over `record Pair(Item: Item)`, `static method Pass<T>(owned a: T): owned T => a;` is therefore rejected at `Pass<Pair>`, its return carrying a borrow of an `owned` parameter, and so are ... and `static method Id<T>(a: T): T where T: value => a;` at `Id<Pair>`; each stays admitted at the declaration and at every substitution that carries no borrow.

title: a where T: value identity is admitted at int, the bullet being read per instantiation
rule: Over `record Pair(Item: Item)`, `static method Pass<T>(owned a: T): owned T => a;` is therefore rejected at `Pass<Pair>`, its return carrying a borrow of an `owned` parameter, and so are ... and `static method Id<T>(a: T): T where T: value => a;` at `Id<Pair>`; each stays admitted at the declaration and at every substitution that carries no borrow.

title: a Box<T> return carrying a plain parameter's borrow is rejected at Wrap<Item>
rule: Over `record Pair(Item: Item)` and `record Box<T>(V: T)`: `static method Wrap<T>(a: T): Box<T> => new Box<T>(a);` is admitted at the declaration and at `Wrap<int>`, and rejected at `Wrap<Item>` by the return bullet, its return carrying a borrow of a plain parameter

title: the same Box<T> return is admitted at Wrap<int>
rule: Over `record Pair(Item: Item)` and `record Box<T>(V: T)`: `static method Wrap<T>(a: T): Box<T> => new Box<T>(a);` is admitted at the declaration and at `Wrap<int>`, and rejected at `Wrap<Item>` by the return bullet, its return carrying a borrow of a plain parameter

title: a generic class storing its T parameter in a T field is rejected wherever Keep<Pair> is named
rule: a `class Keep<T>` whose `Put(a: T)` stores `a` into a `_last: T` field is admitted at the declaration and, under §28.3's field-store bullet, at `Keep<Item>`, and is rejected wherever `Keep<Pair>` is named, by the instance-field bullet, the diagnostic naming the store.

title: a generic class copying T into a field-held Array<T> is rejected wherever Bag<Pair> is named
rule: a `class Bag<T>` whose `Put(t: T)` copies `t` into a field-held `Array<T>` is admitted at the declaration and at `Bag<Item>` (§28.11's store rule, under its residual) and rejected wherever `Bag<Pair>` is named.

title: an override storing its unconstrained type parameter into an Object field is rejected at the body
rule: A dispatched generic method's body decides such a requirement at the body (§14.2). ... a bare `T` stored into an `Object`- or interface-typed field is the same store through §8.6's box at such a substitution.

title: the same override is admitted when the declaring method bounds the parameter to class
rule: A dispatched generic method's body decides such a requirement at the body (§14.2). ... a bare `T` stored into an `Object`- or interface-typed field is the same store through §8.6's box at such a substitution.

title: a span passed at a bare T the call substitutes with Object is rejected
rule: A value that holds borrows may not reach a borrow-erasing position: a position declared `Object` or an interface type — a parameter, plain or `scoped`, a local, a field, a record component, a choice payload, an inline-array slot, a collection slot or collection-literal element, a `ref` or `out` location, a return slot — or a position declared at a bare type parameter that the instantiation substitutes with such a type (`b.Keep<Object>(span)` over `Keep<T>(x: T)`; `xs.Add(span)` at `xs: Array<Object>`).

title: a span added to an Array<Object> is rejected at the conversion
rule: A value that holds borrows may not reach a borrow-erasing position: a position declared `Object` or an interface type — a parameter, plain or `scoped`, a local, a field, a record component, a choice payload, an inline-array slot, a collection slot or collection-literal element, a `ref` or `out` location, a return slot — or a position declared at a bare type parameter that the instantiation substitutes with such a type (`b.Keep<Object>(span)` over `Keep<T>(x: T)`; `xs.Add(span)` at `xs: Array<Object>`).

title: a span is a value type that holds borrows and may not be an async parameter
rule: A value type that holds borrows is stored past its bound at no position: every position whose lifetime its carried borrows' sources do not provably bound — this bullet, the static-field bullet below, the collection bullet's escaping and wider-scoped collections, §30.1's frame rules, §30.5's `Task<T>` row, stdlib §6.5's `AsyncEventSource<T>` payload — is rejected for it statically

title: a closure over a span later reassigned to a local array's span bounds the frame it rides
rule: the capture contributes the sources of the borrows the record carries to the closure's source set, every value the captured binding is assigned, in the enclosing body or in a lambda body, counted ... and the results of invoking it, and every deferred-activation frame or storage-bounded holder it rides, are bounded by them

title: a member store of a same-block using var into a record local is admitted
rule: A record value held at a named location — a local or parameter, a field, a slot of an inline array held at one — is read with one source set ... a member store ... adds the sources of the borrows `e` carries to that set, never removing one, and is checked as an assignment of the updated value to the location that holds it ... so a source declared in the holder's own block or an enclosing one is admitted, as at an inline-array slot

title: a whole-value assignment resets a record local's set before a later member store
rule: A whole-value assignment gives the location the assigned value's set, and a member store ... adds the sources of the borrows `e` carries to that set

title: a member store of an inner-block using var into an outer record local is rejected
rule: A record value held at a named location — a local or parameter, a field, a slot of an inline array held at one — is read with one source set ... a member store ... adds the sources of the borrows `e` carries to that set, never removing one, and is checked as an assignment of the updated value to the location that holds it ... at a local or parameter by §28.3's local-scope bullet

title: a record local carrying a member-stored using var may not be returned
rule: A record value held at a named location — a local or parameter, a field, a slot of an inline array held at one — is read with one source set ... a member store ... adds the sources of the borrows `e` carries to that set, never removing one, and is checked as an assignment of the updated value to the location that holds it ... A borrow-bearing record may be returned only when every borrow it carries has a source the caller re-establishes at the call site

title: a member store at depth through an outer inline array of records from an inner block is rejected
rule: A record value held at a named location — a local or parameter, a field, a slot of an inline array held at one — is read with one source set ... a member store ... adds the sources of the borrows `e` carries to that set, never removing one, and is checked as an assignment of the updated value to the location that holds it ... and at an inline-array slot as §15.1.2's slot store into that array (`a[0].Item := e` over a local `[2]Box` adds to `a`'s one set)

title: a borrow-bearing record with a non-null reference-typed field may not be an instance field (record)
rule: A borrow-bearing record may not be stored in an instance field of a class, except when every reference-typed field is null (the null-source form). The quantifier is over reference-typed fields, not borrow-carrying fields alone: a field whose declared type is reference-typed but not borrow-carrying — a string, a function type — must be null too. new Tok(null, "missing") is rejected even though the borrow-carrying field is null.
check: borrow-bearing record may not be stored in an instance field

title: a borrow-bearing choice with a non-null reference-typed payload may not be an instance field
rule: A borrow-bearing choice may not be stored in an instance field of a class, except when every reference-typed payload is null (the null-source form). The quantifier is over reference-typed payloads, not borrow-carrying payloads alone: a payload whose declared type is reference-typed but not borrow-carrying — a string, a function type — must be null too. Tagged.Named("a", null) is rejected even though the borrow-carrying payload is null.
check: borrow-bearing choice may not be stored in an instance field

title: non-owning inline array of interface in instance field is not a span
rule: A non-owning inline array ([N]T, [N]T?) is an ordinary value type. Its element type being a class or interface does not make the array borrow-bearing or a span. A span may not be stored in an instance field (§9.7); an inline array of a borrow-carrying element type may — it is not a span.

title: a record may not implement IDisposable
rule: Language spec §9.7 (v0.345): "Records cannot have destructors, `owned` fields, or implement `IDisposable` — directly or through an interface extending it, `IAsyncDisposable` among them."

title: a record may not implement an interface that extends IDisposable
rule: Language spec §9.7 (v0.345): "Records cannot have destructors, `owned` fields, or implement `IDisposable` — directly or through an interface extending it, `IAsyncDisposable` among them."

title: a record may not implement IAsyncDisposable
rule: Language spec §9.7 (v0.345): "Records cannot have destructors, `owned` fields, or implement `IDisposable` — directly or through an interface extending it, `IAsyncDisposable` among them."

title: a nested record may not implement IDisposable either
rule: Language spec §9.7 (v0.345): "Records cannot have destructors, `owned` fields, or implement `IDisposable` — directly or through an interface extending it, `IAsyncDisposable` among them." The rule is stated of records as a kind, with no clause limiting it to module-level declarations, so a record declared inside a class is a record too.

title: a record declared in a method body may not implement IDisposable
rule: Language spec §9.7 (v0.350): "Records cannot have destructors, `owned` fields, or implement `IDisposable` — directly or through an interface extending it, `IAsyncDisposable` among them." §21.10 (v0.350) makes a local record "an ordinary nominal record or enum": "every §9 (records) and §10 (enums) rule applies unchanged".

title: a record with only admissible primitive and string components is serialization-eligible
rule: A record or enum is serialization-eligible when it satisfies the synthesis-eligibility rule; declaring the conformance is the opt-in, and the synthesis is automatic when eligible.

title: a record with a class-typed serialized component is not serialization-eligible
rule: A record's serialized components must be record-admissible; a record with a class-typed serialized component is not serialization-eligible, a compile error at the conformance declaration naming the field.

title: serialized skip on a class-typed component rescues serialization-eligibility
rule: serialized skip excludes the component from both directions entirely; a serialized skip component whose type is not defaultable is a compile error, so the remedy uses a nullable class-typed field. The explicit constructor still binds the skipped component: synthesized Deserialize step 2 matches the record's components — the serialized ones together with every `serialized skip` one, which binds its `default(T)`.

title: serialized optional on a non-defaultable enum component is rejected
rule: A serialized optional component whose type is not defaultable is a compile error at the conformance declaration; a missing field would have no value to supply.

title: a record component that declares neither serialization interface is not admissible
rule: A component type is admissible as a serialized component when it is another serialization-eligible record **that itself declares `ISerializable`/`IDeserializable`**: the synthesized members reach the nested value's own `Serialize`/`Deserialize`, which the conformance is the sole source of, so a record shaped eligibly that declares neither interface is not an admissible component and naming one is the conformance-declaration error.

title: the same record component declaring the conformance is admissible
rule: The conformance requirement on the record row is what makes the component encodable: a nested record that declares `ISerializable`/`IDeserializable` supplies the members the synthesized bodies reach, and is then admissible as a serialized component.

title: a serialized rename colliding with another component's name is rejected
rule: The string must be a non-empty literal and must be unique among the serialized names of the type's components; a member's serialized name is its rename where one is declared and its declared identifier otherwise, so a rename equal to another member's identifier collides too. A collision is a compile error at the conformance declaration.

title: an enum is always serialization-eligible and admits a constant rename
rule: Enums are always serialization-eligible. The synthesized form writes the member's serialized name as a string — its `serialized "<name>"` rename where one is declared, its identifier otherwise.

title: a record with a requires-carrying constructor is constructor-only and declares fine
rule: A record type is constructor-only when it declares a constructor carrying a contract clause: a requires clause, an ensures clause, or both, on any constructor of the record, of any visibility, in any recorded tier.

title: default on a constructor-only record is rejected
rule: A constructor-only record is not defaultable; default(R) and every other site that supplies a default(T) are rejected.

title: a constructor-only record does not satisfy where T colon new()
rule: Port at a where T: new() substitution is also rejected.

title: an ordinary body record without a contract-clause constructor satisfies where T colon new()
rule: A value-type substitution satisfies the new() constraint exactly when it is defaultable; a record with no contract-clause constructor is not constructor-only and remains ordinary.

title: a constructor-only record is otherwise ordinary and remains auto-hashable
rule: In every other respect such a record is ordinary; a constructor is a member section 9.2 admits regardless of what its body does, so Port remains auto-hashable, hashable, and serialization-eligible.

title: default initialization of constructor-only-record storage is rejected
rule: A constructor-only record is not defaultable, so default initialization of `R`-typed storage is rejected: the field has no zero value to hold and no constructor behind one.

title: constructor-only-record storage initialized by a constructor call is admitted
rule: The remedy is a constructor or factory call: the property claims provenance — every value of a constructor-only record is produced by a call to one of that record's declared constructors — and a field initializer that calls one satisfies definite assignment.

title: a record declaring positional fields may not declare a contract-clause constructor
rule: A record declaring positional fields may not declare a constructor carrying a contract clause: a compile error at the record declaration. The auto-generated primary constructor carries no clause, so the combination would leave `new R(…)` outside every gate the declared constructor states.

title: default underlying values are assigned 0, 1, 2 in declaration order
rule: This declares constants `Priority.Low`, `Priority.Medium`, `Priority.High` of type `Priority`. The default underlying values are 0, 1, 2 — assigned in declaration order from zero.

title: same-valued constants denote one value under =
rule: Two or more constants of one enum may share an underlying value. Same-valued constants denote one value: `Legacy = Current` is `true`, and no construct can distinguish them at run time.

title: two case arms naming same-valued constants is rejected
rule: In a `case` over the enum, two arms — or two `|` alternatives — naming same-valued constants are a compile error, the later one being unreachable.

title: a case naming only one alias of a shared value is exhaustive and legal
rule: Exhaustiveness is over the set of distinct declared values, so an arm naming either alias covers both.

title: same-valued enum constants draw no diagnostic
rule: Two or more constants of one enum may share an underlying value ... Aliasing is legal and **draws no diagnostic**; exhaustiveness is over the set of distinct declared *values*, so an arm naming either alias covers both.

title: a colon-list head outside the eight integer types is read as an interface, and rejected as one
rule: The colon list is one list: if its first item resolves to one of the eight underlying-type keywords, that item is the underlying type; otherwise the underlying type is `int` and every item names an interface. `double` resolves to none of the eight, so it is read as an attempted interface — and is not one.

title: short is an admitted underlying type
rule: The underlying type must be one of `byte`, `sbyte`, `short`, `ushort`, `int`, `uint`, `long`, `ulong`.

title: FromUnderlyingOrNull returns the declared constant matching the value
rule: `FromUnderlyingOrNull` returns the declared constant whose underlying value equals `value`, or `null` when there is none.

title: FromNameOrNull returns null for a digit string
rule: `FromNameOrNull(name)` returns the declared constant whose identifier equals `name`, or `null` when there is none; a digit string names no constant, since no identifier begins with a digit.

title: NameOf agrees with nameof for a written constant
rule: For a written constant `E.NameOf(E.A) = nameof(E.A)` — `NameOf` extends the compile-time operator to a runtime value over the same table.

title: NameOf yields the first-declared identifier for a shared value
rule: Under duplicate constant values, `NameOf` yields the first-declared constant's identifier for a shared value.

title: a user declaration cannot overload the compiler-provided FromNameOrNull
rule: Every enum carries three compiler-provided static members — `FromUnderlyingOrNull`, `FromNameOrNull`, `NameOf` — and no user declaration, a member or a declared constant, may override or overload any of them.

title: a distinctly named static method beside the compiler-provided tier is admitted
rule: Every enum carries three compiler-provided static members; a user declaration under a different name does not collide with them.

title: an enum's static owned readonly FrozenArray singleton is warning-free
rule: `FrozenArray<Priority>` declares the **immutable** statics-and-sharing fact, placing it in §22.12 rule 4's warning-suppression set — a `static owned readonly` of it is a warning-free, every-domain-readable singleton.

title: the same enum static at a mutable class type draws rule 4's sharing warning
rule: ... where the same field at `Array<Priority>` (a mutable class type outside the set) would draw rule 4's declaration-site sharing warning.

title: an enum cannot declare an instance field
rule: An enum may not declare instance fields (the runtime representation is the underlying integer).

title: a static readonly field is admitted where an instance field is not
rule: An enum may declare `static readonly` fields; instance fields are forbidden because the runtime representation is the underlying integer.

title: an enum cannot declare a block-form property
rule: An enum may declare exactly instance methods, expression-bodied read-only instance properties, static methods, `static readonly` fields, `const` members, and operator overloads — and no others; an enum may not declare block-form properties or properties with backing storage.

title: an enum may declare an expression-bodied read-only instance property
rule: An enum may declare exactly instance methods, expression-bodied read-only instance properties, static methods, `static readonly` fields, `const` members, and operator overloads.

title: override is rejected on an enum member outside the Object-virtual surface
rule: `override` is admitted only on the `Object`-virtual members — `Equals`, `GetHashCode`, `ToString` — and is rejected on every other enum member.

title: override is admitted on ToString
rule: An enum may declare — spelled `override` or plain — `Equals` taking the enum's own type, `GetHashCode(): int`, and `ToString(): string`; each replaces the compiler-generated default for every consumer.

title: overloading homogeneous = on an enum without Equals(T)/GetHashCode is rejected
rule: A record/enum/choice overloading homogeneous `=`/`<>` also declares `Equals(T)` and `GetHashCode` — on an enum, `override` or plain (the co-declaration rule).

title: overloading homogeneous = on an enum together with Equals(T) and GetHashCode is admitted
rule: A record/enum/choice overloading homogeneous `=`/`<>` also declares `Equals(T)` and `GetHashCode` — on an enum, `override` or plain (the co-declaration rule).

title: an override Equals taking Object? on an enum is rejected
rule: An `Equals` taking `Object?` or `Object` is rejected on an enum at the declaration, as on every value kind (§9.2), spelled `override` or plain, the diagnostic naming the own-typed spelling

title: a plain Equals taking Object? on an enum is rejected
rule: An `Equals` taking `Object?` or `Object` is rejected on an enum at the declaration, as on every value kind (§9.2), spelled `override` or plain, the diagnostic naming the own-typed spelling

title: an override Equals taking the enum's own type is admitted
rule: `override` is admitted only on the three `Object`-virtual members the next paragraph names, at exactly the signatures it names — `Equals` taking the enum's own type, `GetHashCode(): int`, `ToString(): string`

title: an enum's own-typed Equals answers direct calls, hash containers and boxed dispatch
rule: Each **replaces the compiler-generated default for every consumer**: direct calls, hash containers (`Set<E>` and `Dictionary<E, V>` reach the user's `Equals`/`GetHashCode`), ..., and virtual dispatch through a boxed reference ([§8.6]) ([§10.5]).

title: a plain Equals at another parameter type replaces nothing; Object.Equals keeps the default
rule: A plain `Equals` at any other parameter type is an ordinary instance method, statically dispatched, that replaces nothing and discharges neither §8.3's pairing nor §25.2's co-declaration obligation ([§10.5]); an enum's default `Equals` is underlying integer equality ([§8.3]).

title: an enum declaring its own-typed Equals without GetHashCode is rejected
rule: A type that overrides `Equals` must also override `GetHashCode`. The compiler enforces this. ([§8.3]); on a value kind whose `Object`-slot `Equals` takes its own type and is declared plain, "a plain `Equals` obliges `GetHashCode`" ([§8.3]), and an enum fills that slot ([§10.5]).

title: an enum with its own-typed Equals and no homogeneous = has no = at its static type
rule: A declared `Equals` also retires the intrinsic `=`: an enum that declares its own-typed `Equals` and no homogeneous `=`/`<>` overload has no `=` or `<>` at all — a use at the enum's static type is a compile error at the expression ([§10.5]).

title: case matching an enum scrutinee admits the omitted prefix and selects the matching arm
rule: Inside a `case` whose scrutinee is an enum, the enum prefix may be omitted.

title: a primary constructor chains to the base via inheritance-clause args
rule: If the class has a base class that requires constructor arguments, the base's arguments appear in parentheses after the base class name in the inheritance list; this desugars to a primary constructor that chains to base(...) before executing field initializers.

title: two base classes on one class is rejected
rule: A class may declare at most one base class and any number of interfaces.

title: a convenience constructor that does not chain to the primary is rejected
rule: A class with a primary constructor may also declare additional constructors in its body using the constructor keyword; such constructors must chain to the primary constructor via this(...).

title: a two-instantiation class answers a generic-body interface call through its instantiation
rule: A generic interface may be listed at **two or more instantiations** (`class D: IComparable<int>, IComparable<string>`), directly or through a base class. The class still declares **one** member set, and [§11.2]'s matching rule is applied once per obligation, each under its own instantiation's substitution ([§11.1]); the call `i.Put(v)` with `v: X` selects the `IL<X>` member `Put(x: X)` ([§22.6]).

title: a one-instantiation class answers a generic-body interface call through that instantiation
rule: The class still declares **one** member set, and [§11.2]'s matching rule is applied once per obligation, each under its own instantiation's substitution ([§11.1]); with the single obligation `IL<int>`, the call `i.Put(v)` with `v: X` selects `Put(x: X)` at `X = int` ([§22.6]).

title: Exception subclasses keep their message through primary and explicit constructors
rule: This desugars to a primary constructor that chains to `base(name, balance)` before executing field initializers ([§11.1]), so the field `Seen: string := Message` of `E(m: string): Exception(m)` reads the message that the base constructor set. The `Exception` surface is "public pure constructor(message: string);" and "public readonly property Message: string;" ([§31.4]). Each of the six checks holds on all 200 iterations: the own message and Show, a rethrown message, a B with its Tag, a D through C (whose constructor chains to A with a `!` appended), and W's `/w` message. So bad stays 0, and the program prints bad=0 and returns 0.

title: a class implements an interface implicitly by declaring matching public members
rule: A class implements an interface implicitly: by declaring matching public members.

title: an interface member may not carry a visibility keyword
rule: Interface members are implicitly public, have no body, and end with `;`.

title: an implementation may widen an interface parameter from T to T?
rule: An implementation may declare a parameter as T? where the interface requires T (the implementation accepts more inputs than the interface promises to pass).

title: an implementation may not narrow an interface parameter from T? to T
rule: The reverse -- interface T?, implementation T -- is rejected, because the implementation would refuse a null the interface promised to accept.

title: owned must match exactly between an interface parameter and its implementation
rule: An implementing method's signature and the interface method's signature must agree on owned as a parameter modifier. Interface declaring M(owned t: T) requires implementation to declare M(owned t: T).

title: a record may not implement an interface declaring a settable member
rule: A record may implement any number of interfaces that declare no settable property or indexer member -- a conformance naming an interface with one is rejected at the declaration (a value kind supplies no receiver-storing accessor).

title: own type parameters inside a generic parameter type match by position, not by name
rule: A member matches an interface member when its parameter types are exactly equal under the interface's substitution, and a member's own type parameters take part by number and position, not by name. Interface P<T, U>(a: Box<T>) is not matched by P<A, B>(a: Box<B>): under the position correspondence T to A and U to B, the interface's parameter is Box<A> and the implementation's is Box<B>.

title: a renamed own type parameter inside a generic parameter type still matches
rule: A member matches an interface member when its parameter types are exactly equal under the interface's substitution, and a member's own type parameters take part by number and position, not by name. Interface P<T>(a: Box<T>) is matched by P<X>(a: Box<X>), and the call through the interface reaches it.

title: a swapped pair of own type parameters inside a generic parameter type is rejected
rule: A member matches an interface member when its parameter types are exactly equal under the interface's substitution, and a member's own type parameters correspond by number and position, not by name. Interface P<T, U>(a: Pair<T, U>) is not matched by P<A, B>(a: Pair<B, A>): the first slot is T (position 1) on the interface and B (position 2) on the implementation.

title: a swapped own type parameter in an owned generic return type is rejected
rule: Return types must match exactly under the interface's substitution, and a member's own type parameters correspond by number and position. Interface P<T, U>(a: T): owned Box<T> is not matched by P<A, B>(a: A): owned Box<B>, because the returned Box's argument is position 1 on the interface and position 2 on the implementation.

title: a function-typed argument with a different arity does not match
rule: Parameter types must match exactly under the interface's substitution. Interface P<T>(a: Array<(T) -> T>) is not matched by P<X>(a: Array<(X, X) -> X>): a two-parameter function type is a different type from a one-parameter function type.

title: a function-typed argument whose return is nullable where the interface's is not does not match
rule: Parameter types must match exactly under the interface's substitution. Interface P<T>(a: Array<(T) -> T>) is not matched by P<X>(a: Array<(X) -> X?>): the nullability exception covers the top level of a parameter, not the return type of a function type nested inside it.

title: a function-typed argument with its own type parameters swapped by position does not match
rule: A member's own type parameters correspond by number and position, not by name. Interface P<T, U>(a: Array<(T) -> U>) is not matched by P<A, B>(a: Array<(B) -> A>): the parameter and return of the function type trade positions.

title: a renamed own type parameter inside a function-typed argument still matches
rule: A member matches an interface member when its parameter types are exactly equal under the interface's substitution, and a member's own type parameters correspond by position, not by name. Interface P<T>(a: Array<(T) -> T>) is matched by P<X>(a: Array<(X) -> X>), and the call through the interface reaches it.

title: a function-typed return with its own type parameters swapped by position is rejected
rule: Return types must match exactly under the interface's substitution, and a member's own type parameters correspond by number and position. Interface P<T, U>(a: T): Array<(T) -> U> is not matched by P<A, B>(a: A): Array<(B) -> A>: the function type's parameter and return trade positions.

title: a bare function-typed return with its own type parameters swapped by position is rejected
rule: Return types must match exactly under the interface's substitution, and a member's own type parameters correspond by number and position. Interface P<T, U>(): (T) -> U is not matched by P<A, B>(): (B) -> A.

title: a swapped own type parameter nested inside a generic parameter type does not match
rule: A member matches an interface member when its parameter types are exactly equal under the interface's substitution, and a member's own type parameters correspond by number and position, not by name. Interface P<T, U>(a: Box<Box<T>>) is not matched by P<A, B>(a: Box<Box<B>>).

title: a swapped own type parameter inside an Array of a generic type does not match
rule: A member matches an interface member when its parameter types are exactly equal under the interface's substitution, and a member's own type parameters correspond by number and position, not by name. Interface P<T, U>(a: Array<Box<T>>) is not matched by P<A, B>(a: Array<Box<B>>).

title: a swapped own type parameter inside a generic over a function type does not match
rule: A member matches an interface member when its parameter types are exactly equal under the interface's substitution, and a member's own type parameters correspond by number and position, not by name. Interface P<T, U>(a: Box<(T) -> T>) is not matched by P<A, B>(a: Box<(B) -> B>).

title: a nullable generic parameter matches a renamed own type parameter and accepts null
rule: A member matches an interface member when its parameter types are exactly equal under the interface's substitution, and a member's own type parameters correspond by number and position, not by name. Interface P<T>(a: Box<T>?) is matched by P<X>(a: Box<X>?), and the call through the interface reaches it.

title: a type alias in a parameter type matches the aliased generic instance
rule: A type alias is a pure synonym, so a parameter declared BI matches a parameter declared Box<int>: the interface's BI and the implementation's Box<int> are exactly equal types. Interface P(a: BI) is matched by P(a: Box<int>), and the call through the interface reaches it.

title: an own type parameter does not match a concrete type argument
rule: A member matches an interface member when its parameter types are exactly equal under the interface's substitution, and a member's own type parameters correspond by number and position, not by name. Interface P<T>(a: Box<T>) is not matched by P<X>(a: Box<int>): the interface's argument is its own parameter, and the implementation's is the concrete int.

title: a zero-argument function type matches a renamed own type parameter
rule: A member matches an interface member when its parameter types are exactly equal under the interface's substitution, and a member's own type parameters correspond by number and position, not by name. Interface P<T>(a: Array<() -> T>) is matched by P<X>(a: Array<() -> X>), and the call through the interface reaches it.

title: a unit-returning function type matches a renamed own type parameter
rule: A member matches an interface member when its parameter types are exactly equal under the interface's substitution, and a member's own type parameters correspond by number and position, not by name. Interface P<T>(a: Array<(T) -> ()>) is matched by P<X>(a: Array<(X) -> ()>), and the call through the interface reaches it.

title: an own type parameter in a function-typed argument does not match a concrete function type
rule: A member matches an interface member when its parameter types are exactly equal under the interface's substitution, and a member's own type parameters correspond by number and position, not by name. Interface P<T>(a: Array<(T) -> T>) is not matched by P<X>(a: Array<(int) -> int>): the interface's function type is generic in its own parameter and the implementation's is concrete.

title: a concrete return type in a function-typed argument does not match an own type parameter
rule: A member matches an interface member when its parameter types are exactly equal under the interface's substitution, and a member's own type parameters correspond by number and position, not by name. Interface P<T>(a: Array<(int) -> T>) is not matched by P<X>(a: Array<(int) -> int>): the interface's return is its own parameter, and the implementation's is the concrete int.

title: a non-generic function-typed argument with a different concrete parameter does not match
rule: A member matches an interface member when its parameter types are exactly equal under the interface's substitution, and a member's own type parameters correspond by number and position, not by name. Interface P(a: Array<(int) -> int>) is not matched by P(a: Array<(string) -> int>): the parameter types are concrete and not exactly equal.

title: a class type parameter substitutes into a function-typed argument of a generic member
rule: A member matches an interface member when its parameter types are exactly equal under the interface's substitution, and a member's own type parameters correspond by number and position, not by name. Under the interface's substitution the class parameter C becomes int, so I<int>'s P<T>(a: Array<(T) -> C>) is matched by P<X>(a: Array<(X) -> int>), and the call through I<int> reaches it.

title: a renamed function-typed return with a renamed own type parameter matches by position
rule: A member matches an interface member when its parameter types are exactly equal under the interface's substitution, and a member's own type parameters correspond by number and position, not by name. Return types must match exactly under the interface's substitution. Interface P<T, U>(a: T): Array<(T) -> U> is matched by P<A, B>(a: A): Array<(A) -> B>: each own parameter corresponds by position, so the renamed names still match, and the call through the interface reaches it.

title: a function-typed return with an own type parameter replaced by a concrete type does not match
rule: Return types must match exactly under the interface's substitution. Interface P<T, U>(a: T): Array<(T) -> U> is not matched by P<A, B>(a: A): Array<(A) -> int>: the function type's return is the own parameter U on the interface and the concrete int on the implementation.

title: a multi-parameter function-typed return with the parameters swapped by position does not match
rule: Return types must match exactly under the interface's substitution. Interface P<T, U>(): (T, U) -> T is not matched by P<A, B>(): (B, A) -> B, because the own type parameters correspond by position, not by name.

title: a curried function-typed return with own type parameters swapped by position does not match
rule: Return types must match exactly under the interface's substitution. Interface P<T, U>(): (T) -> (U) -> T is not matched by P<A, B>(): (B) -> (A) -> B, because the own type parameters correspond by position, not by name.

title: a nullable function-typed return with own type parameters swapped by position does not match
rule: Return types must match exactly under the interface's substitution. Interface P<T, U>(): ((T) -> U)? is not matched by P<A, B>(): ((B) -> A)?, because the own type parameters correspond by position, not by name.

title: a renamed bare function-typed return matches by position
rule: Return types must match exactly under the interface's substitution. Interface P<T, U>(): (T) -> U is matched by P<A, B>(): (A) -> B: the own type parameters correspond by position, so the names need not agree.

title: a class type parameter substituted beside an own type parameter matches
rule: A member matches an interface member when its parameter types are exactly equal under the interface's substitution, and a member's own type parameters correspond by number and position, not by name. The interface's class parameter S is substituted by the implementing class's Z, and the own parameter U corresponds to W by position, so Box<S>, Box<U> matches Box<Z>, Box<W>.

title: a class type parameter beside an own parameter swapped by position does not match
rule: A member matches an interface member when its parameter types are exactly equal under the interface's substitution, and a member's own type parameters correspond by number and position, not by name. Under the substitution S to Z and the position correspondence U to W, the interface's second parameter is Box<W> and the implementation's is Box<Z>; the implementation swaps them.

title: an interface generic argument substituted with the wrong concrete type does not match
rule: A member matches an interface member when its parameter types are exactly equal under the interface's substitution, and a member's own type parameters correspond by number and position, not by name. The interface I<int> substitutes S by int, so its member is P(a: Box<int>); the implementation's Box<string> is not that type.

title: an interface generic argument substituted with the matching concrete type matches
rule: A member matches an interface member when its parameter types are exactly equal under the interface's substitution, and a member's own type parameters correspond by number and position, not by name. The interface I<int> substitutes S by int, so its member is P(a: Box<int>), and the implementation's P(a: Box<int>) matches it; the call through the interface reaches it.

title: a Dictionary parameter with a generic value type matches a renamed own parameter pair by position
rule: A member matches an interface member when its parameter types are exactly equal under the interface's substitution, and a member's own type parameters correspond by number and position, not by name. Interface P<K2, V2>(a: Dictionary<K2, Box<V2>>) is matched by P<A, B>(a: Dictionary<A, Box<B>>): each own parameter corresponds by position.

title: a Dictionary parameter whose own parameters are swapped by position does not match
rule: A member matches an interface member when its parameter types are exactly equal under the interface's substitution, and a member's own type parameters correspond by number and position, not by name. Interface P<K2, V2>(a: Dictionary<K2, Box<V2>>) corresponds by position to P<A, B>(a: Dictionary<B, Box<A>>) only if the key is the first own parameter; here the key is B, so the implementation's parameters are swapped.

title: a nested generic parameter Box of Box matches a renamed own parameter by position
rule: A member matches an interface member when its parameter types are exactly equal under the interface's substitution, and a member's own type parameters correspond by number and position, not by name. Interface P<T>(a: Box<Box<T>>) is matched by P<X>(a: Box<Box<X>>): the single own parameter corresponds by position, so the renamed name still matches.

title: a Pair parameter with renamed own parameters matches by position
rule: A member matches an interface member when its parameter types are exactly equal under the interface's substitution, and a member's own type parameters correspond by number and position, not by name. Interface P<T, U>(a: Pair<T, U>) is matched by P<A, B>(a: Pair<A, B>): each own parameter corresponds by position.

title: an Array of a generic parameter type matches a renamed own parameter by position
rule: A member matches an interface member when its parameter types are exactly equal under the interface's substitution, and a member's own type parameters correspond by number and position, not by name. Interface P<T>(a: Array<Box<T>>) is matched by P<X>(a: Array<Box<X>>): the element type Box<T> under the position correspondence is Box<X>.

title: a generic Box of a function type matches a renamed own parameter by position
rule: A member matches an interface member when its parameter types are exactly equal under the interface's substitution, and a member's own type parameters correspond by number and position, not by name. Interface P<T>(a: Box<(T) -> T>) is matched by P<X>(a: Box<(X) -> X>): the function type is part of the parameter type and corresponds by position.

title: a non-generic zero-argument function type in an Array parameter matches
rule: A member matches an interface member when its parameter types are exactly equal under the interface's substitution, and a member's own type parameters correspond by number and position, not by name. Interface P(a: Array<() -> int>) has no own type parameter; the implementation's parameter is the same type, so it matches and the call through the interface reaches it.

title: a non-generic zero-argument function type with a different concrete return does not match
rule: A member matches an interface member when its parameter types are exactly equal under the interface's substitution, and a member's own type parameters correspond by number and position, not by name. Interface P(a: Array<() -> int>) has parameter type Array<() -> int>; the implementation's Array<() -> string> differs in the function's return type.

title: a concrete function return in a parameter does not match an own parameter in the same slot
rule: A member matches an interface member when its parameter types are exactly equal under the interface's substitution, and a member's own type parameters correspond by number and position, not by name. Interface P<T>(a: Array<(T) -> int>) has the return of its function type fixed to int; the implementation replaces that return with its own parameter X, which is not the same type.

title: a function-typed return with identically named own parameters matches
